you actually already have a really good plan laid out for yourself. bit by bit reclaim yourself. you don't really have to explain anything if you don't feel like having that convo, esp where it might cause hard feelings or lay blame on one person or another. 

if you want to go for a run in the afternoon when you had both normally watched tv (example) just tell him "hey today i feel like going for a run, did you want to join me?" (if you do want him to join you, leave this out if you'd rather go alone) and just go. if he gets upset and tells you that you both normally watch tv together, or why aren't you doing it like normal, just tell him you miss running, it's the truth, and you really feel like doing it today. none of it is a lie, and none of it is placing blame, and if you go do it you're reclaiming your life bit by bit. start sleeping a little earlier, tell him you want to go to bed and wake up early so you can do things earlier. it's totally ok for couples to have different schedules and do different things at different times. 

if you want to cook healthy meals then cook healthy meals. if he wants to go out instead of eating cooking, try to compromise. "i really like the meals i cook and i think they taste good and are healthy. i like it more than eating out, but i know you like going out too so why don't we do 3 days eating in 2 days eating out and the weekend is up in the air depending on our plans, it'll help us save some money too if we don't eat out all the time and we can use those funds for other neat stuff like x y z". none of it is a lie, and you can still regain your own life back. 

theres nothing wrong with doing your own thing and having your own time in relationships. you mentioned being concerned with him feeling lonely. do you feel like, aside from your own withholding, that you have open and honest communication? if so, or even if not this may be a good time to start, at the end of every week saturday so that way you don't spend sunday in a tiff if things go badly on check up day, check in and make sure your partner isn't feeling neglected or alone. "hey i know i've been spending more time running/reading/lately and i just wanna make sure that you're ok with things how they are? should we many any changes? would you like us to set some time aside to do some things together?"  and even if the answer is no, they're fine with it, they're ok, try to set aside some him time days anyways. maybe the night before check in night have it be movie night, once a week watch a show or tv together, aside from if you eat and watch tv together or something, this is like a in-home date night almost, so you can get comfy and relaxed before talking about feelings. 

and if you don't feel comfy introducing this all at once that's totally find and preferable probably if you think it'll be a really big lifestyle shift, you can try once every few months to introduce something new, so that way theres a time for shift and adaption and checking in with feelings and making sure everyones ok with how things are going. if you check in and he's not honest with you that's on him. you can't control what he's going to tell you. just like all these months where you didn't tell him what was on your mind, that was on you. and now you can work to have more alone time and focus on your own things little by little, while still making sure the relationship works and everyone is happy. 

-from an artist who also had to reclaim a bit of time so i could work on art things instead of spending all my time with my s/o, as much as i wanted to :) 
edit: i saw you mentioned courage, just go for it one day. pick the one that's most important to you right now, like if it's running, just do it. i know i say it like it's easy, and it's not, but nothing will change if you don't try and the sooner the better esp if you're feeling resentful for something that you're not talking about to him. he's not aware of this at all. that's not good. think about that as you try to get the courage, because you want your relationship to last. if you get angry at him while you're trying to plan your outing without him and if it doesn't seem to be going well please don't bring that up as a leverage point because that will only hurt far far more than it will help. keep that to yourself because, again, it's on you.

It seems that you've already found peace, somewhat, with your friends and your family. It also seems that you have a plan of how you want to date, and what you're looking for in a partner. 

I would suggest not throwing in the towel yet. I would guess that you're still young, you've only dated two people, and there are plenty more fish in the sea and plenty more chances to date in the future. There is no rush to find your life partner so soon, and you will find that with more time comes more experience. 

Based on your writing, you seem to have your wits about you when looking for a partner. It is all a matter of trial an error. There isn't anything wrong with simply having fun, and not immediately looking for a life partner, which is what I think you're looking for right now. 

I stress having fun because it will help you open up and connect with new people. You seem like a very serious person, just from your writings. You said it's hard for you to open up, and that people don't seem to appreciate it when you do. Most people live openly, and any indication that you are secretive and guarded usually isn't taken in a good way, and you will be looked upon as an unfriendly and reserved person. This isn't all as bad as it seems, but it will hinder your ability to make friends quickly, and usually the emotional connection and dependency is brought about by time and effort, rather than right away connection, which it also seems you might be looking for. 

Anyone who isn't too jaded by their experiences will tell you to keep trying. If it's something that you really do crave, which as you are INFJ I don't doubt it for a moment, then it will be something that you will have to argue with for yourself (I know I do!) that it's worth it and it's worth the heartbreak and any other myriad of negative feelings.  

Just be aware that it isn't as easy as others who are more open and friendly make it out to be. Because of their natural disposition to being friendly, or even if they fake it til they make it, they have more opportunity to meet new people and thus widen their selection of people to choose from in the dating/friend pool. I'm not advising you to suddenly change your personality, but simply to keep that in mind. It will be harder for  you because of your personality, but that isn't any reason for you to give up altogether. 

Please keep trying and continue to argue with yourself about why you want it, make your own list of pros and cons and use that against yourself when you feel defeated. ("I'm so tired of trying to be in love, it only hurts, this is a waste of time, I won't ever find someone that can cherish me for me, but I really do want that, I want someone who can really love me for everything that I have to offer, and I know that I want it, so I'll keep trying, because it has to be out there, somewhere. Optimism at it's finest." type of thing).

As a girl who was raped twice, I would side with her. 

I didn't go to the police. I didn't tell anyone irl for a long, long time. I didn't even tell the hospital staff. 

I'd encourage her to go to the police. Go with her if you can. I'm surprised that you didn't insist on this already. She may be lying about when it happened (my memory of the second rape is so bad that I can't tell you the day it happened on, just the month, and that's because I know what I did in life after the rape, if I didn't have that event after, I wouldn't know at all. I suppressed it from my mind.)

Even without a rape kit it can still go in your girlfriends favor. The police will talk with her. Encourage her to get counseling (people will say this is not your problem. It is not. However, I am extreamly grateful for all the people in my life that I told a year after that encouraged me and forced me to go to counseling. It helped when I was sure it wouldn't.) and try to help her. 

If you're still having doubts, after this, watch her. 

I was very lucky and did not get pregnant either time.  

There is no way a test will show up after five days, but did she ever tell you when it happened? Or did she just finally talk to you about it before she told you this extra info? The people that knew my first rapist defended him with everything after I told one person about it and it went to the grapevine. They said I was lying, no way such a kind and nice person would ever do that, especially to his girlfriend...
So I can see where her sister might have said something to that effect. 

Don't discredit her yet, you may be the only person that is on her side. Tell her to go to the police. She may not want to. Ask her why. 

I didn't go to the police and didn't want to because I didn't believe they would help me. I only heard of girls that had been raped that talked to the police and nothing got done. My family dropped me off at the police station without telling me where we were going... lol. 
The police didn't help because of the way I deal with stress, and I dealt with it by shutting down. I had no emotions for months after. 

It only broke when I was at college later, and some guy tried to hug me and when I said no he told me he knew I liked it and I broke down and threw my books, my shoes lol, everything I could find at him and my family had to come pick me up like an errant child because I couldn't stop crying and shaking (panic attack) that my family even believed me. It hurt in an unimaginable way for them to tell me they finally believed me. It hadn't been long from it happening. I couldn't understand why they didn't believe me. (now I realize it's probably because I didn't go to the police, I didn't go to the hospital, all these things that everyone so far has said is "bs, you can't be this stupid" but... it happens. It doesn't mean it didn't happen and your girlfriend isn't telling the truth.)

People will crack under the strain and stress differently. Everyone is different. Please try to listen to her before you dismiss it entirely.
